To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a competitive network is described that learns to recognize invariant objects on the basis the spatio temporal correlations in a sequence of images; 2) the network learns to recognize objects on the basis spatio temporal correlations, which are not invariant to translation, rotation, and size; 3) the network is able to recognize objects on basis of spatio temporal correlations which are not invariant, because of its ability to learn the correlations between the current and the previous neural activity; 4)

a) the proposed network can learn invariant recognition of objects in a manner that is superior to the Neocognitrons, b) the proposed network learns invariant recognition by using spatiotemporal correlations, and c) the proposed network uses a learning rule which is based on the Hebb's rule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of object recognition, which we define as the task of classifying an unknown object into a set of known classes on the basis of the information provided by the sensory input.
the development of a model of invariant object recognition in which the learning is unsupervised and is achieved through the use of a competitive Hebb like rule.
developing an artificial neural network that can learn to recognize invariant objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the network presented in this thesis is a viable candidate for an unsupervised learning algorithm for invariant object recognition.
this work is an excellent example of a successful attempt to use spatio-temporal correlations for learning.

the proposed method has been shown to be capable, on two different tasks, of outperforming the Neocognitrons supervised version, and that it is a viable alternative to the supervised Neocognitronics supervised version.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the network is a competitive network that learns to classify objects by using spatio temporal correlations.
we have shown that the use of spatio-temporal correlations in learning invariant object recognition is a powerful tool.
the network is capable of learning invariant object recognition on the basis of spatiotemporal correlations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a competitive learning rule, which is dependent upon both prior and current neural activity, can be used for invariant object recognition.
the Hebb-like learning rule can outperform the supervised rule in the cross-validation test.
a competitive network can outperform a supervised network on the cross validation task of invariant object recognition, given a small training set.
